title: Driver + CUDA range profiles and snapshotting for reproducible benchmarks
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: We see intermittent performance variance across nightly benchmark runs (tokens/sec drift and p95 latency spikes) that correlate with different GPU driver and CUDA combinations and nondeterministic runner startup state. Goal: Define a compact, supported matrix of driver + CUDA ranges, capture deterministic runtime snapshots (pinned images + seedable runner configs), and add automated verification to nightly pipelines to detect regressions before merging runtime changes. Deliverables: 1) Driver+CUDA range matrix document and an accepted compatibility policy; 2) A snapshot artifact format (image + metadata + seed manifest) that can be stored and reused by CI; 3) A test harness that runs a canonical tokens/sec and p95 workload under each snapshot and emits a regression signal to our alerting dashboard; 4) CI gating threshold definitions (relative and absolute) and remediation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published to Confluence and linked from benchmark CI
Snapshot artifacts produced by infra pipeline and uploaded to S3 with immutable tags
Nightly benchmark job runs snapshot list and posts metrics to metrics cluster with regression checks enabled
Regression alerts trigger a PR Auto-block and create ENG issue when threshold exceeded
Runbook documented: how to repro locally from snapshot and how to bisect driver vs model vs runner changes
steps_to_reproduce: Start runner with --seed-file and --pinned-image flags per manifest
Run canonical workload: 500 concurrent short-context chat requests and 100 long-context streams
Collect tokens/sec and p95 latencies via our bench-exporter and compare against baseline
If tokens/sec drops >6% or p95 increases >20% relative to baseline, create regression_event alert
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Agreed to support driver ranges rather than single pinned driver to reduce patch churn (decision by runtime and infra leads)
2025-02-20: Chose S3 artifact + JSON metadata manifest over OCI artifact alone so we can include seed and kernel-version hints (approved)
2025-02-25: Thresholds for automated regression: default 6% tokens/sec drop OR 20% p95 increase OR 3 consecutive nightly violations (configurable per-model)

notes: We intentionally support ranges (eg cuda>=11.7 && cuda<=12.2) to allow minor driver updates while keeping reproducibility via snapshot manifests.
Include a small 'sanity' workload that exercises KV cache warm start to detect kernel-level regressions even when tokens/sec appears stable.
Work with SRE to ensure we can retain snapshots for 90 days by default; longer retention for archived regressions.
Plan to add a 'simulation' run mode that replays recorded request traces deterministically against snapshot to narrow nondeterminism sources.
